# B1 — Down syndrome univariate baselines {#sec-appendix-b1}

## VG01 — Words spoken (worked exemplar) {#sec-appendix-vg01}

VG01 instantiates the shared engine (@sec-betabinomial, @sec-kappa, @sec-mean, @sec-anchors, @sec-hsgp) for a single outcome — words spoken by children with Down syndrome — out of $N_{\text{trials}} = 800$ words, with reference ages $x_a = 24$ and $x_b = 84$ months and no extension mechanisms. It is presented in full here as the worked exemplar; later entries cite these sections rather than repeating them.

### Model-specific priors

Anchoring the linear trend (@sec-anchors) at 24 and 84 months. Previous research and professional experience suggest many children with Down syndrome say very few words at 24 months, with substantial uncertainty up to ~100 words, and a wide range of ability by 84 months:

| Parameter | Description | Prior |
|----|----------------|------------|
| $p_{24}$ | Expected proportion of words spoken at 24 months | $\mathrm{Beta}(1, 15)$ |
| $p_{84}$ | Expected proportion of words spoken at 84 months | $\mathrm{Beta}(1.1, 1.1)$ (≈ uniform) |

: VG01 slope-anchor priors (all other priors per @tbl-core-priors). {#tbl-vg01-priors}

![Prior for the lower slope anchor (spoken words at 24 months)](figures/VG01-age-spoken-ds/p_slope_low_dist.png){#fig-vg01-slope-low width="5in"}

![Prior for the upper slope anchor (spoken words at 84 months)](figures/VG01-age-spoken-ds/p_slope_hi_dist.png){#fig-vg01-slope-hi width="5in"}

### Dispersion: a worked example {#sec-vg01-kappa}

VG01 makes the age-varying dispersion of @sec-kappa concrete. For the Down syndrome data the age standard deviation is $s_x \approx 24$ months, so a one-unit change in standardised age ($\Delta z = 1$) is about two years. Writing $\log(\kappa(z) - \kappa_{\min}) = a_\kappa + b_\kappa z$, the coefficient $b_\kappa$ is the log-multiplicative rate of change in the *excess* concentration per SD of age, and for any $\Delta z$,

$$
\frac{\kappa(z+\Delta z) - \kappa_{\min}}{\kappa(z) - \kappa_{\min}} = \exp(b_\kappa\,\Delta z).
$$

With $b_\kappa = -b_{\mathrm{mag}}$ and the shared prior $b_{\mathrm{mag}} \sim \mathrm{HalfNormal}(0.3)$ (@tbl-core-priors), a typical magnitude is on the order of $0.3$, i.e. a multiplicative change of $\exp(-0.3) \approx 0.74$ — about a 26% decline in excess concentration per SD of age (roughly two years), tapering toward the floor $\kappa_{\min}$ at older ages (more between-child heterogeneity later). The dispersion priors are shown below.

![`kappa_min` prior (dispersion floor).](figures/VG01-age-spoken-ds/kappa_min_dist.png){#fig-vg01-kappa-min width="4in"}

![`a_kappa` prior (log-scale intercept).](figures/VG01-age-spoken-ds/a_kappa_dist.png){#fig-vg01-a-kappa width="4in"}

![`b_kappa_mag` prior (decline rate magnitude).](figures/VG01-age-spoken-ds/b_kappa_mag_dist.png){#fig-vg01-b-kappa width="4in"}

### Prior predictive checks

Before fitting, we checked that the priors generate plausible age–vocabulary curves: low counts at younger ages, increasing expected counts across childhood, smooth month-to-month change rather than abrupt oscillation, and a widening between-child spread at later ages without implausible mass near impossible values. The prior predictive draws (@fig-vg01-prior-samples, @fig-vg01-prior-ppc) confirm the priors are informative enough to encode basic developmental expectations while leaving substantial uncertainty about the shape of the trajectory.

![Prior sample trajectories (VG01).](figures/VG01-age-spoken-ds/prior_samples.png){#fig-vg01-prior-samples .lightbox fig-align="left"}

![Prior predictive checks (VG01).](figures/VG01-age-spoken-ds/prior_predictive_checks.svg){#fig-vg01-prior-ppc .lightbox fig-align="left"}
